title: Niche-Encoded Medicinal Nature A Hierarchical Generative Framework for Qi Nature, Five Flavors, and Meridian Tropism in Chinese Materia Medica
content: Background: Qi nature (si qi), the five flavors (wu wei) and meridian tropism (gui jing) are the core descriptive categories of Chinese materia medica. Their origin remains contested between two readings: an epiphenomenon of chemical composition, or an untestable residue of philosophical terminology. This study asks whether these properties admit a unified account that requires neither costly compositional assay nor abandonment of quantitative testability.Methods: A master table of 1045 materia medica and food records was combined with four independent classes of evidence: WorldClim continuous climate surfaces; ERA5-Land root-zone soil moisture (29 daodi producing regions, 166 records); the primary text of the Song-dynasty Zhenglei Bencao; and the taste-to-potency rules of Ayurveda and Tibetan medicine. Analyses used out-of-fold cross-validation, phylogenetic whitening, two-way variance decomposition, within/between-group decomposition, 1000-fold permutation, Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and cross-dynasty concordance tests.Results: (1) Explanatory power of the two objective physical classes was low throughout, with only 4.2%-4.5% remaining significant at item level after BH correction; at producing-region level the maximum of 14.0% before correction fell to q = 0.071 and was no longer significant. (2) Variance decomposition placed 93.6% of qi-nature variance between species (196 species, 453 records; ICC(1) = 0.888), and 52.8% between producing regions (138 regions, 432 records; ICC(1) = 0.310); cross-granularity comparison rests on ICC(1) (0.888 and 0.310), the eta-squared values not being group-size-adjusted, and among 36 species recorded in two or more regions, 86.1% (31/36) carry an identical qi nature across regions, indicating that regional differences largely project species composition. (3) Recognizable habitat classes were instead strongly associated with qi nature: 17 classes, Cramer's V = 0.6064 (chi-square = 414.1, df = 32, p = 5.45x10⁻⁶⁸, n = 563); at the two ends of the four habitat belts 7 of 269 records (2.6%) ran opposite to expectation, 206 (76.6%) fell on the expected side and 56 (20.8%) were recorded neutral, a non-contradiction rate of 97.4%; and all 60 fungal records were neutral. (4) After phylogenetic whitening, three poles emerged: cold-bitter, neutral-sweet, warm-pungent (pungent p approx 10^-27; bitter and sweet p approx 10^-13). (5) Two-way decomposition showed that the weights of the two predictive pathways differ by taste: for pungency the label pathway (partial eta-squared = 0.2445) exceeded the habitat pathway (0.0253) by 9.7-fold; for saltiness the reverse held (0.0085 vs 0.0448, 5.3-fold); for bitterness the two were nearly equal (0.0740 vs 0.0703). The label pathway is proxied by taste presence, and the functional channel still lacks an independently observable variable. (6) Cross-system comparison converged on pungent, bitter and sweet, while saltiness showed substantive opposition: within the aquatic group the salty-versus-non-salty difference of -0.25 was not significant (p = 0.144), whereas within the non-aquatic group salty records were markedly colder (-0.28 vs +0.09, difference -0.37, p = 0.015). This opposition is reported, not resolved. (7) At the meridian level the increment from the five flavors was essentially zero (-0.015 to +0.012), and only the hepatic morphological-part signal survived four correction regimes (delta AUC = 0.098). (8) Across roughly 500 years, directional concordance for 178 substances was 77.5% with Cohen's kappa = 0.493, i.e. moderate agreement.Conclusions: Qi nature and the five flavors can be accounted for by two channels, habitat endowment and functional effect, with a reliability best described as directionally testable and rankable, but neither probability-calibrated nor sufficient for continuous numerical prediction; strong prediction of meridian tropism awaits double-blind re-annotation. The failure of objective physical variables is not due to insufficient measurement precision but to a mismatch of observational unit: grids are indexed by locality, medicinal nature by species.
